newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Taiwan rules out Hong Kong-style reunification.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan rules out Hong Kong-style reunification.

text.p: Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang called on China on Thursday to renounce the use of force against the island and said there was no chance of it following Hong Kong's example of reunification with the mainland.
"There is no support in Taiwan for a reckless or precipitate reunification at the moment," Chang told the European Parliament during an address that has infuriated China.

Chang, grandson of the late Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek, told a packed gathering of the Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee that formulas such as "One State Two Systems" were "inapplicable and unacceptable to Taiwan".
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since the Communists won the Chinese civil war and drove Chiang Kai-shek and his defeated Nationalists into exile in Taiwan in 1949.
China considers Taiwan a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation in a quest to bring Taiwan under its rule.
Chang said Taiwan's goal was to be recognised as an independent member of the international community coexisting peacefully with its giant mainland communist rival.

"Beijing should give peace a chance," he said, stressing President Lee Teng-hui had indicated a willingness on several occasions to travel to Beijing or "anywhere else to hold talks with Communist leaders".
Taiwan's trade with the European Union rose to $31.3 billion in 1996 with most going to Germany, the Netherlands, France and Italy.
China has slammed the European Parliament, a vociferous critic of the communist state's human rights policy, for inviting Chang, saying the move was gross interference in China's internal affairs.

"We express our firm opposition and strong indignation to this," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said when asked to comment on Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang's scheduled address to the European Parliament in Brussels on Thursday.
"This seriously encroaches upon China's sovereignty and is also gross interference in China's internal affairs," he said.
